message:
docs(field-test): the 720p that never came back, and the loop that explains it

At 17:56:08 the host put the profile back to high at 12 Mbps and logged
encode=1280x720 in the same line. The budget returned; the resolution did not.
The viewer saw its last 1920x1080 at 17:55:21.557 and 1280x720 from .763
onward, unbroken to the end of the log.

The code path closes a loop. Frame payload dimensions are written into
encodeSource unconditionally, while the corrective ApplyTarget that would
refit runs only when the aspect ratio has moved -- and 1280x720 and 1920x1080
are both 16:9, so the anti-thrash guard lowers the source and skips the
correction. From there fit_size_preserving_aspect caps scale at 1.0 and clamps
to the source, so asking for 1080p yields 720p forever. The confirmed-geometry
path already refuses that skip, in a comment explaining exactly this hazard.

What this is not: a measurement. No log carries encodeSource at runtime, so
the most that is claimed is that the code admits the loop and the field
observations agree with it. Agreement is not proof, and the drop/FEC/NACK
counters are recorded as the fields they are, not as a loss rate.

Filed as HN13. Not fixed -- and allowing upscale unconditionally would not be
the fix, since it would stretch genuinely smaller sources.

Separate from the 17:16 silence; different event, different document.

Documentation only -- read-only NAS access, no product change, no build, no
live session touched. Note that viewer.log rotated mid-investigation and the
oldest generation was lost.
